errors.why: The Tibetan asks the Mīmāṃsaka to establish a FAULTLESS author (skyon med byed po), not an erroneous one.
snying rje is compassion (karuṇā), not equanimity.

errors.english: Therefore, I utterly reject that, and I have no great interest in it.
errors.why: The author says he has no great inclination to refute it at length (hence 'who would obstruct what is not needed now?'), not that he rejects it and has no interest in it.

note: Generally follows the anti-Mīmāṃsā verse argument, but one slip inverts 'faultless author' and karuṇā is mistranslated.

errors.why: In context 'sogs pa' sets out the enumerated items (colour etc.), as the gloss that follows says; a Sāṃkhya position is out of place in this discussion of cowness.

note: A careful rendering of a dense lemma-and-gloss commentary on universals; one doubtful reading.
Faithful rendering of the Tibetan verses (the Sanskrit lines are parallel text); the imagery and the goddess's speech are correct.

errors.english: Being blue, he is the son of that father, because of being it, like the other appearing.
errors.why: This is the stock inference 'he is dark, because he is that man's son, like the other [son] seen': darkness is the thesis and sonship the reason, which the English scrambles.

fix.find: Being blue, he is the son of that father, because of being it, like the other appearing.
fix.replace: He is dark, because he is that father's son, like the other [son] who is seen.

errors.english: however they are of the nature of non-existence, because they are not observed however they are
errors.why: ji ltar yang means 'in some respect / somehow' (the qualified-predication examples), not 'however they are'; the rendering obscures the argument.

errors.english: Does this reason possessing this characteristic cause realization generally
errors.why: rtogs bya asks whether the reason is itself to be ascertained in general, not whether it causes realization.

note: Literal and often opaque; the key example inference is garbled and the qualified-predication examples are hard to follow.
Accurate rendering of Avalokitavrata on cetanā/cetayitvā karma, with the root-text quotations correctly set off.

span_why: The opening glosses (rjes su mthun pa'i gnas, ri sul, gnas shing spyod pa, de nas, ri'i khrod, de na ni) before 'stag mo ni' are not translated.

errors.why: yid gcugs means trusting/confident (viśvasta), which is why it is glossed 'without suspicion'; it does not mean loving.

errors.english: though steadfast, fell under the power of compassion
errors.why: The quoted root verse is the lemma being commented on, but it is put into a bracketed translator's note rather than given as the quoted text.

note: The word-by-word glosses on the tigress episode are rendered correctly, but the side's opening is missing.

errors.english: This is not the case; if it were to possess parts
errors.why: de lta ma yin te here means 'otherwise' (if it had parts it would not be a substance), supporting the preceding claim rather than rejecting it.

errors.english: In order to demonstrate the meaning of the scripture
errors.why: mdo here is the root verse of the treatise that the author (Dignāga) explains in his own commentary, not a scripture.

errors.english: a school of ancient Indian philosophy that asserts the reality of atoms and substances
errors.why: An unmarked explanatory gloss is inserted into the running translation.

note: Sound rendering of Vinītadeva on atoms and conventional existence, with minor argumentative and framing slips.

errors.english: the relation of inherence or conjunction
errors.why: ldan pa is conjunction (saṃyoga); inherence is 'du ba (samavāya), which the text treats separately right after.

note: Follows the argument on svabhāva/tadutpatti versus conjunction-based reasons faithfully; the notes are mostly helpful.

errors.english: the object of inference is said to exist
errors.why: dmigs pa here is perception/observation (the image is perceived), not an object of inference.

fix.find: the object of inference is said to exist

errors.english: Because it clarifies the nature of what is unapprehended through the power of consciousness, it thinks that such appearances exist.
errors.why: This whole clause belongs to the opponent's single thought (waking cognition reveals that the dream content is unreal, while its appearance is due to the power of consciousness); the English splits it and makes the agent unclear.

note: The dream/rebirth argument is broadly followed, but there is a wrong term for dmigs pa and the opponent's position is muddled.

errors.english: enters and rises from cessation, secluded from desires
errors.why: The Tathāgata enters the FIRST DHYĀNA (secluded from desires, etc.) and rises from cessation; the English makes cessation the state that is secluded and possesses joy.

fix.find: enters and rises from cessation, secluded from desires, secluded from unwholesome, non-virtuous states, accompanied by coarse investigation and subtle analysis, and possessing the joy and bliss born of seclusion, which is the first concentration.
fix.replace: enters the first concentration, which is secluded from desires, secluded from unwholesome, non-virtuous states, accompanied by coarse investigation and subtle analysis, and possessing the joy and bliss born of seclusion, and rises from cessation.

errors.why: The sentence continues 'rnam par dag par' from the previous side: it is the cause of sentient beings becoming purified, not a 'transformation'.

note: Most of the cause/condition list is right, but the dhyāna/cessation sequence is garbled.
